title: Record linked-payer and self-hosted-agent contracts without adopting a second authority or runtime
problem: Anthropic introduced request-level linked billing and a self-hosted Managed Agents stack that materially change payer, storage, orchestration, credential, security, residency, retry, and cost boundaries. Decide whether to amend protocol law, adopt either feature, record evidence only, or make no repository change.
baseline: Default routes are local-first. DALEOBANKS alone retains optional legacy OpenAI Chat Completions and embeddings. No Anthropic linked billing, self-hosted Managed Agents, OpenAI Workspace Agent or Costs API, or Kimi runtime was found. Draft PR 105 section 7 already governs exact contracts, leased state, canonical receipts, retries, cost, independent evaluation, credentials/data scope, and duplicate runtimes.

alternatives.name: Evidence-only update
alternatives.description: Add the dated packet and this deliberation; change no protocol text or runtime.
advantages: Preserves new payer and runtime-boundary contracts
alternatives.revival_evidence: Selected because request-level payer choice and a self-hosted provider agent loop/database/worker stack cross the materiality gate.

alternatives.name: Brief only
disadvantages: Loses durable evidence in the established provider-review lineage
alternatives.revival_evidence: Use for cycles without a breaking contract, hard deadline, material incident, direct exposure, or new authority/runtime boundary.

alternatives.name: Vendor-specific protocol amendment
alternatives.description: Add named Anthropic linked-billing and self-hosting clauses.
disadvantages: Couples constitutional text to volatile products
alternatives.revival_evidence: A deterministic failure demonstrates an invariant missing from section 7.

alternatives.name: Immediate adoption
alternatives.description: Link customer billing or deploy self-hosted Managed Agents now.
advantages: Could shift spend to customers or add deployment control
disadvantages: No need, consent design, account contract, security proof, benchmark, cost baseline, or founder approval exists
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder-approved sandbox with pinned contracts, least privilege, independent acceptance, total-cost ceiling, and rollback.

alternatives.name: Provider-native authority and runtime
alternatives.description: Let provider payer, session, database, queue, worker, retry, and evaluator state own collaboration.
disadvantages: Violates canonical authority, one-source-of-truth, evaluator independence, and no-duplicate-runtime constraints
alternatives.revival_evidence: None while UNIIMENTE requires one canonical authority, task, receipt, evidence, cost, and consequence plane.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Brief the user and leave PR 105 unchanged.
disadvantages: Loses durable payer-selection and self-hosted-runtime evidence

roles.position: Keep provider payer state, sessions, agents, queues, tools, and histories subordinate to human authority and one canonical machine.
material_concerns: A customer billing link must not become canonical consent or authority
Self-hosting must not legitimize a second scheduler or source of truth

roles.position: Bind payer and self-hosted execution contracts to canonical tasks, attempts, receipts, topology, and postconditions.
material_concerns: Unlink or cap changes can silently change payer and retry semantics
Worker polling, restart, queue races, and partial tools make completion ambiguous

roles.position: Make no repository change because direct feature exposure is negative and section 7 already covers the invariants.
material_concerns: Five role prompts are one model's self-review
Provider pages can change after capture
evidence_refs: Negative searches on four default branches

roles.position: Record the contracts but deploy nothing until necessity, ownership, isolation, recovery, and total cost are proven.
material_concerns: Managed Agents requires database, worker, sandbox, backup, and credential operations
Payer errors and delayed telemetry can create support burden and duplicate spend

roles.position: Treat linked billing, session state, status, and cost data as bounded evidence requiring consent, privacy review, and independent reconciliation.
material_concerns: Self-hosting storage does not prove local inference or residency
Billing links can expose customer and organization relationships
The provider cannot solely certify its own payer allocation or execution
evidence_refs: Anthropic self-hosted Managed Agents security and credential boundaries

evidence.claim: Anthropic introduced linked billing with request-level payer selection.
evidence.finding: Release dated 2026-11-17; every Messages or Chat Completions request can carry billing_policy after a customer links a direct-billed organization. No direct repository exposure found.

Release dated 2026-11-12; operators own service, database, workers, shell isolation, credentials, persistence, and operations while inference data can still leave the deployment. No direct repository exposure found.

evidence.claim: Provider agent, cost, model, meeting, and latency incidents occurred in the review window.
evidence.finding: OpenAI Workspace Agent start and delayed-cost incidents; Anthropic model and Meetings incidents; Kimi TTFT incidents from 2026-11-11 through 2026-11-17. No affected direct route found.

evidence.claim: No other material OpenAI or Kimi platform change affected current repository surfaces.
evidence.finding: OpenAI's specialized CSAM moderation model has no current route; Kimi's latest platform release group remained October.

evidence.claim: Current default branches lack direct exposure to the material new features.
evidence.reference: GitHub exact searches at Kernel d64a6c93, DALEOBANKS 667439f4, WMI ec82b802, PumpStation db6758df on 2026-11-17
evidence.finding: DALEOBANKS retains optional gpt-4o-mini Chat Completions and text-embedding-3-small only; no payer policy, Managed Agents service, Costs API, Anthropic, or Kimi runtime found.

counterevidence.claim: New constitutional protocol text is necessary.
counterevidence.finding: Existing provider-neutral rules cover every observed invariant.

counterevidence.claim: Official documentation proves UNIIMENTE or account behavior.
counterevidence.reference: No provider account, credential, billing link, invoice, contract, deployment, or live call was accessed
counterevidence.finding: Integration behavior and non-repository exposure remain unknown.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Preserve one canonical, retry-safe, independently evaluated, privacy- and cost-bounded collaboration runtime while recording actionable payer and self-hosting contracts.

advantages.statement: Dated evidence captures request-level payer selection, unlink/cap transitions, and the self-hosted agent service's storage, queue, worker, shell, credential, and inference boundaries.
advantages.amplified_value: Future owners can test or reject these features from official contracts without adopting them now.

advantages.statement: Provider-neutral rules absorb new billing and deployment products without constitutional churn.
advantages.amplified_value: Canonical authority remains stable across changing vendors, payer models, databases, queues, and worker topologies.

disadvantages.statement: Another weekly record increases review debt.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Add two unique evidence files and one bounded PR-body delta only.

disadvantages.statement: The new provider features have no direct default-branch exposure.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Label exposure negative and defer code, deployment, and account action until authorized use exists.

disadvantages.statement: Payer unlink/cap transitions and missing policy can create unsafe replay or double charging.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Require exact payer binding, no silent fallback, canonical receipts, and independent reconciliation before retry.

disadvantages.statement: Self-hosted workers, queues, restarts, and partial tools can create duplicate effects or a second runtime.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Require one canonical scheduler, attempt/receipt mapping, isolated workers, effect reconciliation, and explicit replacement-or-adapter architecture.

disadvantages.statement: Self-hosting can be mistaken for local inference, ZDR, or residency assurance.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Trace every storage and network boundary; require provider-region, retention, and ZDR evidence before data use.

disadvantages.statement: One model's structured five-role review is not independent approval.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep draft status and require founder or delegated independent review.

comparisons.baseline: Local-first defaults, optional legacy OpenAI calls, no Anthropic/Kimi route, generic provider controls.
comparisons.do_nothing: Avoids review debt but loses durable payer-selection and self-hosted-runtime evidence.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: User brief only; lower burden but weak for the established official-source evidence lineage and the new duplicate-runtime boundary.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Provider payer state, sessions, database, queues, workers, retries, and evaluators own collaboration; convenient but incompatible with canonical authority, consent, and evaluator independence.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: If authorized, replay frozen payer-transition and Managed Agents restart/duplicate/partial-effect fixtures offline, then run a cost-capped isolated sandbox with no external consequence and independent acceptance.

rejected_alternatives.name: Add vendor-specific law
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A deterministic failure proves an uncovered invariant.

rejected_alternatives.name: Link billing or deploy now
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: No authorized need, account contract, consent design, isolation proof, benchmark, total-cost review, or founder approval exists.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Authorized need plus pinned fixtures, least privilege, independent evaluation, total-cost review, and rollback.

rejected_alternatives.name: Inspect accounts, credentials, or invoices
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: This review lacks authority to access provider accounts, secrets, policies, billing connections, projects, or invoices.

pass_2.attack_summary: The evidence-only design can become bureaucracy, overstate one-model review, rely on mutable pages, miss non-repository use, normalize provider payer state as authority, or let self-hosting disguise a second runtime and remote data path.

new_weaknesses.statement: The recurring draft can become harder to review than the risk.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Keep this cycle to two evidence files and one body section; no protocol or code change.

new_weaknesses.statement: Linked billing and Managed Agents can make provider identity, spend controls, session state, queues, and retries architectural dependencies.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Retain canonical consent, budgets, tasks, receipts, and scheduler; forbid provider-owned authority or evaluation.

new_weaknesses.statement: Provider docs, status, beta headers, and service behavior can change after capture.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Preserve dates, URLs, exact branch SHAs, and require a fresh contract check before implementation.

new_weaknesses.statement: Infrastructure, database, worker, sandbox, egress, inference, tools, duplicate work, support, and billing corrections can hide total cost.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require a complete total-cost model and kill adoption when any material cost is unavailable.

new_weaknesses.statement: A self-hosted database may be misrepresented as data residency while model content and identifiers still leave the deployment.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require end-to-end data-flow, retention, region, ZDR, deletion, and credential-boundary evidence.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: New payer and duplicate-runtime boundaries justify one evidence-only update.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Next cycle; brief-only unless materiality is met

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: No adapter, deployment, billing link, or migration is built until authorized exposure exists.
Exact payer binding, no-fallback semantics, canonical receipts, and independent reconciliation are required before retry.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any link, unlink, cap, payer, authorization, or billing error transition

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: No service, database, queue, worker, shell, scheduler, runtime, or tool is deployed or activated.
Local storage is explicitly insufficient; end-to-end residency, retention, ZDR, and deletion evidence is required.
Five roles are labelled self-review and cannot authorize adoption or merge.

pass_2.final_design: Add only the 2026-11-17 official-source evidence packet and validated deliberation to draft PR 105; leave section 7 and all runtime, routes, accounts, credentials, billing links, production, authority, and default branches unchanged.

residual_risks.mitigation: Require a separate authorized inventory before any adoption or migration.

residual_risks.risk: The deliberation is not independent approval.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep draft status and require founder or delegated human decision.

residual_risks.risk: Provider contracts can change after capture.
residual_risks.mitigation: Recheck official sources and pin fixtures before any canary.

dissent.handling: Preserve the brief-only objection. It controls scope: no protocol text, runtime code, fixture, provider call, deployment, account inspection, billing link, or migration. Request-level payer choice and a self-hosted provider agent loop/database/worker stack justify only dated evidence.

entries.position: Make no repository change because direct feature exposure is negative and existing rules are sufficient.
entries.rationale: Recurring model-authored records can create bureaucracy and de facto policy authority.
entries.evidence_threshold: Future updates require direct exposure, a hard effective transition, breaking contract, material incident, or uncovered authority/runtime invariant.
entries.review_trigger: Founder review or next weekly cycle

migration_plan: No runtime or billing migration. If exposure is authorized, pin provider/API/beta/model/region/payer/application/connection/cap/service/license/database/worker/sandbox/tool/retention contracts; map every payer transition, session, phase, model call, tool effect, retry, and cost into canonical attempts and receipts; prove disconnect, cap, restart, duplicate delivery, partial effect, persistence loss, revocation, outage, and reconciliation with deterministic fixtures; perform independent evaluation and consent/credential/residency/retention/total-cost review; then run a founder-approved sandbox.

steps: Leave draft PR 105 unmerged or revert only the 2026-11-17 evidence commits
Preserve evidence and dissent as historical records
Return to brief-only reporting for immaterial cycles

kill_criteria: Any default-branch write or unapproved merge
Any account link, credential, production, routing, spending, deployment, or authority change
Any silent payer fallback, payer substitution, or double charging
Any provider billing connection treated as canonical consent, identity, authorization, budget, or cost truth
Any self-hosted provider session, database, queue, worker, history, receipt, retry, evaluator, cost plane, scheduler, or runtime treated as canonical
Any retry or failover without receipt, effect, payer, and idempotency reconciliation
Any shell/file worker without container or VM isolation and least privilege
Any local-storage claim used as residency, retention, deletion, or ZDR proof
Any missing infrastructure, database, sandbox, egress, inference, tool, retry, or support cost
review_trigger: Founder review of PR 105; any Anthropic linked-billing or self-hosted Managed Agents proposal; any provider incident with ambiguous completion, payer allocation, or delayed cost
